---
    name: 'build images'
    
    on:
      push:
        branches:
          - master
          - test
        tags:
          - '*'
    concurrency:
      group: ci-image-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}-${{ github.repository }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.runs-on }}
        strategy:
          # Images are independent - one failing build must not cancel the others.
          fail-fast: false
          matrix:
            include:
              - name: kairos-orin
                context: ./kairos-orin-docker
                dockerfile: ./kairos-orin-docker/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-orin
                platform: linux/arm64
                runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
              - name: kairos-thor
                context: ./kairos-thor-docker
                dockerfile: ./kairos-thor-docker/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-thor
                platform: linux/arm64
                runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
              - name: kairos-dgx-spark
                context: ./kairos-dgx-spark-docker
                dockerfile: ./kairos-dgx-spark-docker/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-dgx-spark
                platform: linux/arm64
                runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
              - name: l4t-unsloth
                context: ./l4t-unsloth
                dockerfile: ./l4t-unsloth/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/l4t-unsloth
                platform: linux/arm64
                runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
              - name: github-runner
                context: ./github-runner
                dockerfile: ./github-runner/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/github-runner
                platform: linux/amd64
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
              - name: kairos-wifi
                context: ./kairos-wifi
                dockerfile: ./kairos-wifi/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-wifi
                platform: linux/amd64
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
              - name: kairos-wifi-ubuntu
                context: ./kairos-wifi-ubuntu
                dockerfile: ./kairos-wifi-ubuntu/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-wifi-ubuntu
                platform: linux/amd64
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
              - name: kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu
                context: ./kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu
                dockerfile: ./kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu
                platform: linux/amd64
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
              - name: openstam
                context: ./openstam
                dockerfile: ./openstam/Dockerfile
                image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/openstam
                platform: linux/amd64
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Set up QEMU
            uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@master
            with:
              platforms: all
          - name: Set up Docker Buildx
            id: buildx
            uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@master
    
          - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
            if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
              registry: ghcr.io
              username: ${{ github.actor }}
              password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - name: Extract metadata (tags, labels) for Docker
            id: meta
            uses: docker/metadata-action@2a4836ac76fe8f5d0ee3a0d89aa12a80cc552ad3
            with:
              images: ${{ matrix.image }}
              tags: |
                type=semver,pattern={{raw}}
                type=ref,event=branch
              flavor: |
                latest=auto
                prefix=
                suffix=
    
          - name: Build
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
            with:
              builder: ${{ steps.buildx.outputs.name }}
              context: ${{ matrix.context }}
              file: ${{ matrix.dockerfile }}
              platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
              push: true
              tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
              labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}

---
name: 'build ISOs'

# Builds bootable installer ISOs from the Kairos OS images, each on a runner of
# its own architecture (no qemu). Run manually (workflow_dispatch) to get ISOs as
# artifacts, or on a published release to also attach the ISOs to that release.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Image tag to build the ISO from'
        default: 'master'
        required: true
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: write   # upload ISO assets to the release
  packages: read    # pull the images from ghcr
  actions: read     # poll the 'build images' run for this commit

concurrency:
  group: isos-${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  iso:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runs-on }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: kairos-thor
            image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-thor
            arch: arm64
            runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
          - name: kairos-dgx-spark
            image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-dgx-spark
            arch: arm64
            runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
          - name: kairos-wifi-ubuntu
            image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-wifi-ubuntu
            arch: amd64
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Resolve image tag
        id: meta
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Free disk space + pick a work dir with room
        id: workdir
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /opt/hostedtoolcache /usr/local/share/boost 2>/dev/null || true
          docker system prune -af >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          df -h
          # ISO assembly needs ~15-20GB; prefer /mnt if it has more free space
          mnt_free=$(df -P /mnt 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $4}' || echo 0)
          cwd_free=$(df -P . | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
          if [ "${mnt_free:-0}" -gt "${cwd_free:-0}" ]; then
            D=/mnt/isobuild; sudo mkdir -p "$D"; sudo chmod 777 "$D"
          else
            D="$PWD/out"; mkdir -p "$D"
          fi
          echo "dir=$D" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Log in to ghcr.io
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # A release fires this workflow and 'build images' off the same tag, one
      # second apart, but an image build takes hours - 2h54m for v1.2.0. The old
      # 15-minute pull retry could never outlast that, so kairos-thor logged
      # `manifest unknown` 30 times and v1.2.0 shipped with no ISO at all. Wait
      # for the image build at this same commit to finish before pulling.
      #
      # Any conclusion ends the wait, not just success: 'build images' runs its
      # matrix with fail-fast: false, so a sibling image failing says nothing
      # about this one. The pull below is what decides, and it now fails in 5
      # minutes instead of grinding for 15.
      - name: Wait for the images build at this commit
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 14400 ))   # 4h; a full matrix runs ~3h
          while :; do
            # `|| true`: run: blocks are `bash -e`, and one transient API blip
            # must not kill a four-hour wait. An empty reply reads as 'missing'
            # and we simply poll again.
            run=$(gh api \
              "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/images.yaml/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=1" \
              --jq '.workflow_runs[0] // {} | [.status // "missing", .conclusion // "-", .html_url // "-"] | @tsv' \
              || true)
            status=$(printf '%s' "$run" | cut -f1)
            # gh writes its error body to STDOUT, so on a 404 or a rate limit
            # $status is a lump of JSON. Anything that is not a real run status
            # (including empty) is treated as 'not there yet' and re-polled.
            case "$status" in
              queued|in_progress|requested|waiting|pending|completed) ;;
              *) status=missing ;;
            esac
            conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$run" | cut -f2)
            url=$(printf '%s' "$run" | cut -f3)
            if [ "$status" = "completed" ]; then
              echo "build images completed ($conclusion): $url"
              if [ "$conclusion" != "success" ]; then
                echo "::warning::build images concluded '$conclusion'; pulling anyway, this image may be missing"
              fi
              break
            fi
            if [ "$status" = "missing" ]; then
              echo "no 'build images' run for $SHA yet; waiting..."
            else
              echo "build images is $status: $url"
            fi
            if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
              echo "timed out after 4h waiting for the images build at $SHA"; exit 1
            fi
            sleep 60
          done

      - name: Pull image
        run: |
          IMG="${{ matrix.image }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}"
          for a in $(seq 1 10); do
            docker pull "$IMG" && exit 0
            echo "pull attempt $a failed (registry propagation?); retrying in 30s..."
            sleep 30
          done
          echo "image $IMG never became available"; exit 1

      - name: Build ISO with auroraboot (native, no qemu)
        run: |
          IMG="${{ matrix.image }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}"
          DIR="${{ steps.workdir.outputs.dir }}"
          CNAME="auroraboot-${{ matrix.name }}-${{ github.run_id }}"
          # v0.23.0 sometimes HUNG in post-build cleanup *after* writing the
          # ISO, so `docker run` never returned and the job sat until the 6h
          # GitHub limit. v0.27.1 exits cleanly on the same input, but the cap
          # stays: it costs nothing on a healthy run and it bounds a hang we
          # have already paid for once. A real build is a few minutes, so a 20m
          # cap only trips on the hang, by which point the ISO is complete.
          # --name lets us force-remove the container even though `timeout` only
          # kills the docker CLI client, not the container it spawned.
          set +e
          timeout 1200 docker run --rm --name "$CNAME" --privileged \
            -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$DIR":/output \
            quay.io/kairos/auroraboot:v0.27.1 build-iso --arch ${{ matrix.arch }} \
            --output /output --override-name ${{ matrix.name }} \
            docker:"$IMG"
          rc=$?
          set -e
          docker rm -f "$CNAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          # auroraboot runs as root and re-owns the output dir to root:root, so
          # reclaim it before the runner (unprivileged) writes the checksum and
          # the upload step reads the artifacts.
          sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$DIR"
          if ! ls "$DIR"/*.iso >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! file "$DIR"/*.iso | grep -q "ISO 9660"; then
            echo "auroraboot failed (rc=$rc): no complete ISO produced"; exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "auroraboot exited rc=$rc but a valid ISO exists (post-build cleanup hang); continuing"
          fi
          ( cd "$DIR" && sha256sum *.iso > "${{ matrix.name }}.iso.sha256" )
          ls -lh "$DIR"

      - name: Upload ISO artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.name }}-${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}-iso
          path: |
            ${{ steps.workdir.outputs.dir }}/*.iso
            ${{ steps.workdir.outputs.dir }}/*.iso.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Attach ISO to the release
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # --repo is not optional here: this workflow has no actions/checkout,
          # so gh cannot infer the repository from a git remote and v1.2.0 died
          # with "failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository" *after* the
          # ISO had already built and uploaded as an artifact.
          gh release upload "${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}" \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            "${{ steps.workdir.outputs.dir }}"/*.iso \
            "${{ steps.workdir.outputs.dir }}"/*.iso.sha256 --clobber

# kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu: Kairos image with a gfx1151-fixed kernel

Date: 2026-09-29
Status: design, awaiting review

## Problem

`strix` (AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S, gfx1151) runs an older build of
`kairos-wifi-ubuntu` (Kairos v3.5.9, kernel `6.14.0-36-generic`, MES firmware
0x80). Under ROCm llama.cpp load its GPU hangs and resets: 80 resets in the 6
days up to 2026-09-29. 72 of them start with the same kernel message:

```
amdgpu: MES failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE
amdgpu: MES might be in unrecoverable state, issue a GPU reset
```

The reset kills every GPU process. The LocalAI backend exits with
`HW Exception by GPU node-1 ... reason :GPU Hang`, the frontend evicts the
model, and requests fail.

Root cause: the gfx1151 compute wave save/restore (CWSR) area is sized too
small. The kernel fix is two commits:

- `drm/amdkfd: bump minimum vgpr size for gfx1151` (cf326449637a5)
- `drm/amdkfd: Export the cwsr_size and ctl_stack_size to userspace`

They are in mainline 6.18.4+, the Ubuntu OEM 6.14 and 6.17 kernels, and the
6.17 HWE kernel. `6.14.0-36-generic` does not have them. A running kernel with
the fix exports `cwsr_size` and `ctl_stack_size` in
`/sys/class/kfd/kfd/topology/nodes/*/properties`, and strix exports neither.

The MES "LR compute workaround" (MES firmware >= 0x7f plus
`drm/amdgpu: Enable MES lr_compute_wa by default`) was an earlier attempt at a
fix. Upstream removed it in February 2026 because the VGPR fix was the real one.

Current mitigation: `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` is set on strix through
`extra_cmdline` in `/oem/grubenv` (applied 2026-09-29).

References:

- ROCm/ROCm#5590: same hardware, MES 0x80, same messages; workaround `cwsr_enable=0`
- ROCm/ROCm#5724: MES 0x83 causes page faults and GPU hangs on gfx1151
- ROCm/ROCm#6165: silent hard hang with MES 0x86 on gfx1151
- Ubuntu kernel-team SRU "GFX1151 kernel fixes", January 2026
- Launchpad #2129150: MES firmware >= 0x7f for the LR compute workaround

## Goal

Build an OS image for strix whose kernel has the gfx1151 CWSR fix, so strix
runs with the default `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=1` and has no MES hangs.

Success criteria:

1. On strix, `uname -r` shows the OEM kernel from the image.
2. `cwsr_size` and `ctl_stack_size` appear in the kfd topology of the GPU node.
3. `/sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/cwsr_enable` reads `1`, and `/oem/grubenv`
   has no `extra_cmdline`.
4. During 24 hours of normal LLM load, `journalctl -k` shows no
   `MES failed to respond` and no `GPU reset`, and no LocalAI backend exits
   with `GPU Hang`.
5. The rest of strix still works after the upgrade: Wi-Fi, time sync, NAS
   mount, zram, all pods Running, and `https://notary.nervhq.ai/api/auth/status`
   returns 200.

## Non-goals

- Changing `kairos-wifi-ubuntu`. Other boxes that use it keep their kernel.
- Moving the gfx1151 MES blobs to a newer version. The fix is in the kernel,
  and newer MES blobs (0x83, 0x86) have had their own gfx1151 bugs. The image
  pins the blobs strix runs now (see "MES firmware").
- Ubuntu 26.04 or a mainline kernel.
- Baking `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` into the image.

## Design

### Image layout

New directory `kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu/`, separate from `kairos-wifi-ubuntu`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `Dockerfile` | Based on `kairos-wifi-ubuntu/Dockerfile`, with the kernel steps below |
| `time-sync.yaml` | Copy of `kairos-wifi-ubuntu/time-sync.yaml` |
| `custom_bind_mounts.yaml` | Copy of `kairos-wifi-ubuntu/custom_bind_mounts.yaml` |
| `firmware/` | Pinned MES blobs, their `SHA256SUMS`, and `LICENSE.amdgpu` |
| `check-image.sh` | The build checks. Takes a root directory, so tests can run it against fake roots |
| `tests/check-image_test.sh` | Tests for `check-image.sh` with good and bad fake roots |

The image does not use `FROM kairos-wifi-ubuntu`: two images that depend on
each other would have to build in order in CI. The two copied YAML files are
the cost of that choice.

The pins stay the same as `kairos-wifi-ubuntu`: `quay.io/kairos/kairos-init:v4.3.0`,
`ubuntu:24.04`, `VERSION=v4.3.0`, `K8S_PROVIDER=k3s`,
`K8S_VERSION=v1.34.11+k3s1`. If the existing "Check Kairos release pins" CI
step checks a list of images, add the new image to that list.

### Kernel

In the `base-kairos` stage:

1. Run `/kairos-init -s install --skip-step installKernel`, with the same
   provider and version flags as `kairos-wifi-ubuntu`.
2. Run `apt-get install -y linux-oem-24.04`.
3. Remove every kernel image, module and header package that is not the OEM
   kernel, so the image has exactly one `/boot/vmlinuz-*`. Kairos boots
   `/boot/vmlinuz`, so the kernel it boots must be the OEM one.
4. Run `/kairos-init -s init`, which builds the initramfs for the OEM kernel.

If `kairos-init` does not accept `--skip-step installKernel` in v4.3.0, use the
fallback: let it install its kernel, install `linux-oem-24.04`, remove the
kernel packages that are not the OEM kernel, and then run `init`. The build
checks below catch a wrong kernel in both cases.

The final stage is the same as in `kairos-wifi-ubuntu`: `network-manager`,
`wpasupplicant` and `iw` with `--no-install-recommends`, then the two
`/system/oem` YAML files.

### MES firmware

The image vendors the two gfx1151 MES blobs that strix runs now (MES 0x80,
MES_KIQ 0x6f, from noble `linux-firmware 20240318.git3b128b60-0ubuntu2.21`)
into `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/`. The kernel loads firmware from
`updates/` before `/lib/firmware/amdgpu/`.

Reasons (found while writing the plan, 2026-09-29):

- The MES version is not in the file. The `mes_ucode_version` header field of
  strix's `gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin` is `0`. The kernel reports `0x80` because it
  reads the version from the running MES. A build check cannot read the
  version from the file.
- Noble now ships the AMD blobs in `linux-firmware-amd-graphics`
  (`0ubuntu3.3`), and its `gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin` is a different file
  (sha256 `762addfa…`) from strix's (`8e07832c…`). Its version is unknown
  until it runs, and it can be the bad 0x83.
- With the pinned blobs, the upgrade changes only the kernel.

The blobs are redistributable under `LICENSE.amdgpu` from upstream
linux-firmware. The image ships that license next to them.

### Build checks

A check script that runs as the last `RUN` step of the Dockerfile. If a check
fails, the build fails and CI pushes nothing.

1. **Exactly one kernel.** `/lib/modules` has one directory, and its name
   ends in `-oem`.
2. **The kernel has the fix.** The installed `linux-modules-<ver>` changelog
   contains both `drm/amdkfd: bump minimum vgpr size for gfx1151` and
   `drm/amdkfd: Export the cwsr_size and ctl_stack_size to userspace`.
   Verified: the `6.17.0-1032-oem` changelog lists both, and strix's
   `6.14.0-36-generic` changelog lists neither. A string search in
   `amdgpu.ko` does not work: both kernels contain `cwsr_size`.
3. **The pinned MES firmware is in place.** The decompressed
   `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst` and
   `gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst` match the pinned sha256 values. If the initramfs
   contains `amdgpu.ko`, it also contains the two `updates/` blobs.

### Documentation

- `README.md`: add a `kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu` row to the Images table, and a
  `### Kairos Strix Halo (Ubuntu)` section after `### Kairos WiFi (Ubuntu)`.
  The section says why the image exists (gfx1151 CWSR fix), which kernel it
  ships, how to upgrade (`kairos-agent upgrade --source oci:...`), and that
  `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` is not needed with it.
- The Dockerfile header comment explains the kernel choice in the same style as
  the other Kairos Dockerfiles.

### CI

`.github/workflows/images.yaml` needs a matrix entry like the
`kairos-wifi-ubuntu` one:

```yaml
- name: kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu
  context: ./kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu
  dockerfile: ./kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu/Dockerfile
  image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}/kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu
  platform: linux/amd64
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

That file has uncommitted local changes that are not part of this work. The
implementation does not commit it. It gives the entry to the owner, who adds
it together with their own change.

## Rollout on strix

Change one thing at a time. Each step has a way back.

1. **Build and publish.** The image builds locally with its checks passing, and
   then CI publishes `ghcr.io/mudler/dockerfiles/kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu:master`.
2. **Upgrade with the workaround still set.** On strix, run
   `sudo kairos-agent upgrade --source oci:ghcr.io/mudler/dockerfiles/kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu:master`
   and reboot. `extra_cmdline=amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` stays in `/oem/grubenv`,
   so this step changes only the OS image. The previous image stays on the
   passive partition as a boot fallback.
3. **Check the new image.** Check success criteria 1, 2 and 5. Also check that
   the image's `/system/oem/time-sync.yaml` and the hand-placed
   `/oem/92_time-sync.yaml` do not both install and start a clock-step service.
   If they conflict, remove `/oem/92_time-sync.yaml`, because the image now
   provides it.
4. **Remove the workaround.** Run
   `sudo grub2-editenv /oem/grubenv unset extra_cmdline` and reboot. Check
   criterion 3.
5. **Soak test.** Run 24 hours of normal load, then check criterion 4.
   - If it passes, go to step 6.
   - If it fails, run
     `sudo grub2-editenv /oem/grubenv set extra_cmdline="amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0"`,
     reboot, and investigate again. strix stays on the new image.
6. **Record it.** In `infra-flux-kube`, update `docs/services.md`: strix runs
   `kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu`, and the CWSR workaround is gone.

Rollback of the image: boot the passive (fallback) entry, or run
`kairos-agent upgrade` with the previous image reference.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| `linux-oem-24.04` points to a kernel without the fix, or to a kernel that is too new | Build check 2 fails the build |
| A noble `linux-firmware` update ships MES 0x83 | The image pins the known-good 0x80 blobs in `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/`, and build check 3 checks them |
| The OEM kernel lacks a module strix needs | Verified: `linux-modules-6.17.0-1032-oem` contains `mt7925e` (strix Wi-Fi), `zram`, `cifs`, `overlay`, `br_netfilter` and `vxlan` |
| The Kairos v3.5.9 to v4.3.0 upgrade breaks OEM config (`/oem/9x_*.yaml`) | Step 3 checks NAS, zram, time sync and Wi-Fi. The A/B fallback keeps the old image |
| The ROCm userspace in the LocalAI image reads the new `cwsr_size` and behaves differently | Criterion 4 covers this. The step 5 fallback restores the known-good state |
| The OEM kernel has a different amdgpu memory default (GTT/VRAM) | Step 3 compares `mem_info_vram_total`, `mem_info_gtt_total` and `MemTotal` with the values from before the upgrade (96GiB VRAM, about 15.5GiB GTT, about 31GiB RAM) |

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: github-runner
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: github-token
  namespace: github-runner
stringData:
  token: XXX
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: github-runner
  namespace: github-runner
  labels:
    app: github-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: github-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: github-runner
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 100

### Kairos WiFi (Ubuntu)

A Kairos image for a standard amd64 machine (laptop, NUC, mini-PC) that needs to
join a wireless network. Built through the Kairos 4.3.0 BYOI path on Ubuntu
24.04 with k3s, so it installs and upgrades like any other Kairos node:

```bash
kairos-agent upgrade --source oci:ghcr.io/mudler/dockerfiles/kairos-wifi-ubuntu:master
```

Where [Kairos WiFi](#kairos-wifi) is openSUSE with `iw` and `wpa_supplicant`
only, this one adds a NetworkManager-driven stack:

- `network-manager` (`nmtui` / `nmcli`), installed without recommends
- `wpasupplicant` and `iw`

WiFi firmware is not added: the Kairos Ubuntu base already carries
`linux-firmware`, so the image grows by only the WiFi userspace.

Join a network on the box with `nmtui`. The connection is saved under
`/etc/netplan` (Ubuntu's NetworkManager writes connections as netplan yaml) and
`/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections`, both bind-mounted onto the persistent
partition, so it survives OCI upgrades that replace the rootfs.

The image also carries a one-shot NTP clock step (`/system/oem/time-sync.yaml`),
and it is not optional on a WiFi box. NetworkManager owns the wireless device,
so systemd-networkd treats it as unmanaged, `systemd-timesyncd` never sees the
network come online and sends **zero** NTP packets. The clock keeps whatever the
RTC held, every TLS handshake fails with "certificate has expired or is not yet
valid", and the box cannot pull a single container image — k3s could not even
pull its own pause image. The one-shot steps the clock over raw SNTP once the
network is up, retrying and time-bounded so it can never hang the boot.

Wired networking is untouched. Kairos configures ethernet through
systemd-networkd and rewrites its DHCP files on every boot; Ubuntu's
NetworkManager ships `unmanaged-devices=*,except:type:wifi,...`, so it only ever
claims the wireless device and the two never contend. That default is also what
keeps NetworkManager away from the interfaces k3s creates (`cni0`, `flannel.1`,
veths) — do not override it in `/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d`.

A bootable installer ISO is built by the `build ISOs` workflow (run it manually,
or take it from a release) — useful here, since the machine may have no wired
port to install over.

### Kairos Strix Halo (Ubuntu)

`kairos-wifi-ubuntu` for the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151),
with two changes:

- **The kernel is `linux-image-oem-24.04`** (6.17 OEM), not the kernel
  kairos-init installs. On the stock noble kernel the GPU hangs under ROCm
  load (`MES failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE`, then a GPU reset). The
  cause is a gfx1151 CWSR save area that is too small. The OEM kernel has the
  fix, so this image does not need `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0`.
- **The gfx1151 MES firmware is pinned** to the MES 0x80 blobs in
  `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/`. Newer gfx1151 MES blobs have had their
  own hangs. See [`kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu/firmware/README.md`](kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu/firmware/README.md).

The build runs `check-image.sh` and fails if the kernel does not have the
fix or the pinned firmware is missing. To test the check script:

```bash
sh kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu/tests/check-image_test.sh
```

Upgrade a running Kairos node:

```bash
kairos-agent upgrade --source oci:ghcr.io/mudler/dockerfiles/kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu:master
```

After the reboot, the fix is active if the GPU node exports the CWSR sizes:

```bash
grep -E 'cwsr_size|ctl_stack_size' /sys/class/kfd/kfd/topology/nodes/*/properties
```

# Pinned gfx1151 MES firmware

These are the MES blobs that strix (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151) ran without
problems before this image. The kernel reports them as `MES 0x80` and
`MES_KIQ 0x6f`. They come from noble
`linux-firmware 20240318.git3b128b60-0ubuntu2.21`.

The image installs them in `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/`. The kernel loads
firmware from `updates/` before `/lib/firmware/amdgpu/`, so noble firmware
updates cannot replace them.

Why they are pinned:

- The MES version is not in the file (the header field is `0`). You only see
  the version after the kernel loads the blob.
- Newer gfx1151 MES blobs have had their own bugs: 0x83 causes page faults
  (ROCm/ROCm#5724) and 0x86 causes silent hangs (ROCm/ROCm#6165).

To change a blob, boot it on strix, read the version with
`sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/*/amdgpu_firmware_info | grep MES`, run a
load test, and then update `SHA256SUMS` and the pins in `../check-image.sh`.

License: `LICENSE.amdgpu`.

#!/bin/sh
# Tests for ../check-image.sh. Each case builds a fake image root in a temp
# directory and checks the exit code and the failure message.

set -eu

here=$(unset CDPATH; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
check="$here/../check-image.sh"
fw="$here/../firmware"
kver=6.17.0-1032-oem
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
failures=0

vgpr_line='  * drm/amdkfd: bump minimum vgpr size for gfx1151'
export_line='  * drm/amdkfd: Export the cwsr_size and ctl_stack_size to userspace'

# make_root DIR: a root that passes every check.
make_root() {
    r=$1
    mkdir -p "$r/lib/modules/$kver" "$r/usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver" \
        "$r/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu" "$r/boot"
    printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "linux-oem-6.17 ($kver)" "$vgpr_line" "$export_line" |
        gzip -c > "$r/usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver/changelog.Debian.gz"
    cp "$fw/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst" "$fw/gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst" \
        "$r/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/"
    echo kernel > "$r/boot/vmlinuz-$kver"
    ln -s "vmlinuz-$kver" "$r/boot/vmlinuz"
    echo initrd > "$r/boot/initrd"
}

# fake_lsinitrd FILE CONTENT: a script that prints CONTENT, used as LSINITRD.
fake_lsinitrd() {
    printf '#!/bin/sh\ncat <<"EOT"\n%s\nEOT\n' "$2" > "$1"
    chmod +x "$1"
}

# Default initramfs listing: built for the OEM kernel, without amdgpu.
fake_lsinitrd "$work/ls-default" "usr/lib/modules/$kver/kernel/fs/overlayfs/overlay.ko.zst"
LSINITRD=$work/ls-default
export LSINITRD

expect_pass() {
    name=$1; root=$2
    if out=$("$check" "$root" 2>&1); then
        echo "ok   $name"
    else
        echo "FAIL $name: expected pass, got: $out"; failures=$((failures + 1))
    fi
}

expect_fail() {
    name=$1; root=$2; want=$3
    if out=$("$check" "$root" 2>&1); then
        echo "FAIL $name: expected failure, got: $out"; failures=$((failures + 1))
    elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -Fq "$want"; then
        echo "ok   $name"
    else
        echo "FAIL $name: wanted '$want', got: $out"; failures=$((failures + 1))
    fi
}

r=$work/good; make_root "$r"
expect_pass "good root" "$r"

r=$work/no-initrd; make_root "$r"
rm "$r/boot/initrd"
expect_fail "missing initrd" "$r" "initramfs /boot/initrd not found"

r=$work/initrd-other-kernel; make_root "$r"
fake_lsinitrd "$work/ls-other" "usr/lib/modules/6.14.0-36-generic/kernel/fs/overlayfs/overlay.ko.zst"
LSINITRD=$work/ls-other expect_fail "initrd built for another kernel" "$r" "initramfs is not built for $kver"

r=$work/vmlinuz-dangling; make_root "$r"
rm "$r/boot/vmlinuz-$kver"
expect_fail "vmlinuz symlink to a missing kernel" "$r" "/boot/vmlinuz-$kver not found"

r=$work/two-kernels; make_root "$r"
mkdir -p "$r/lib/modules/6.8.0-90-generic"
expect_fail "two kernels" "$r" "expected exactly one kernel"

r=$work/generic; make_root "$r"
mv "$r/lib/modules/$kver" "$r/lib/modules/6.14.0-36-generic"
expect_fail "generic kernel" "$r" "is not an -oem kernel"

r=$work/no-changelog; make_root "$r"
rm "$r/usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver/changelog.Debian.gz"
expect_fail "missing changelog" "$r" "changelog not found"

r=$work/no-vgpr; make_root "$r"
printf '%s\n' "$export_line" |
    gzip -c > "$r/usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver/changelog.Debian.gz"
expect_fail "changelog without vgpr fix" "$r" "bump minimum vgpr size for gfx1151"

r=$work/no-export; make_root "$r"
printf '%s\n' "$vgpr_line" |
    gzip -c > "$r/usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver/changelog.Debian.gz"
expect_fail "changelog without export fix" "$r" "Export the cwsr_size and ctl_stack_size"

r=$work/fw-missing; make_root "$r"
rm "$r/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst"
expect_fail "missing firmware" "$r" "gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst"

r=$work/fw-tampered; make_root "$r"
printf 'not the pinned blob' | zstd -q -f -o "$r/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst"
expect_fail "tampered firmware" "$r" "gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst does not match"

r=$work/vmlinuz-other; make_root "$r"
echo other > "$r/boot/vmlinuz-6.8.0-90-generic"
ln -sfn vmlinuz-6.8.0-90-generic "$r/boot/vmlinuz"
expect_fail "vmlinuz points elsewhere" "$r" "/boot/vmlinuz is not vmlinuz-$kver"

r=$work/vmlinuz-copy; make_root "$r"
rm "$r/boot/vmlinuz"; cp "$r/boot/vmlinuz-$kver" "$r/boot/vmlinuz"
expect_pass "vmlinuz is a copy of the OEM kernel" "$r"

r=$work/initrd-ok; make_root "$r"; echo initrd > "$r/boot/initrd"
fake_lsinitrd "$work/ls-ok" "usr/lib/modules/$kver/kernel/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu.ko.zst
usr/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst
usr/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst"
LSINITRD=$work/ls-ok expect_pass "initrd has amdgpu and pinned firmware" "$r"

r=$work/initrd-no-amdgpu; make_root "$r"; echo initrd > "$r/boot/initrd"
fake_lsinitrd "$work/ls-noamd" "usr/lib/modules/$kver/kernel/fs/overlayfs/overlay.ko.zst"
LSINITRD=$work/ls-noamd expect_pass "initrd without amdgpu" "$r"

r=$work/initrd-bad; make_root "$r"; echo initrd > "$r/boot/initrd"
fake_lsinitrd "$work/ls-bad" "usr/lib/modules/$kver/kernel/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu.ko.zst
usr/lib/firmware/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst"
LSINITRD=$work/ls-bad expect_fail "initrd has amdgpu but not the pinned firmware" "$r" "initramfs has amdgpu.ko but not updates/amdgpu/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst"

r=$work/initrd-no-tool; make_root "$r"; echo initrd > "$r/boot/initrd"
LSINITRD=/nonexistent/lsinitrd expect_fail "initrd but no lsinitrd" "$r" "cannot list the initramfs"

if [ "$failures" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "$failures test(s) failed"; exit 1
fi
echo "all tests passed"

# jetson/common and jetson/t234, both signed by /usr/share/keyrings/jetson-ota.gpg.
# An L4T package installed later in the same stage puts the stock file back, and
# the restored copy is the flash-time template: its SOC entry is still the literal
# placeholder, never substituted for this board.
#
# That single resurrected file caused every failure seen so far. Unqualified
# duplicates of jetson/common made apt refuse to read the whole source list
# ("Conflicting values set for option Signed-By ... The list of sources could not
# be read", exit 100); with that resolved, the placeholder entry then 404'd
# ("The repository 'https://repo.download.nvidia.com/jetson/<SOC> r36.4 Release'
# does not have a Release file"), which is equally fatal to apt-get update.
#
# Removing it restores exactly what kairos-init intended. Nothing is lost: the
# AGX Orin currently in the fleet, running the previous published-base image,
# carries only jetson/common and jetson/t234 — the same two repos
# nvidia-drivers.list provides, and no jetson/ffmpeg.
#
# The greps are deliberate: this cannot be reproduced off an arm64 L4T rootfs, so
# if the layout ever changes the build log shows the before/after state rather
# than failing blind.

    echo "--- jetson apt sources before ---"; \
    grep -rn "repo.download.nvidia.com" /etc/apt/ || true; \
    rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-l4t-apt-source.list; \
    echo "--- after dropping the stock L4T list ---"; \
    grep -rn "repo.download.nvidia.com" /etc/apt/ || true; \
    apt-get update

# Update and install dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    vim \
    htop \
    tmux && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

    curl \

    curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc && \
    chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc && \

    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \

    docker-ce-cli \
    containerd.io \

    docker-compose-plugin && \

```markdown
# Pinned gfx1151 MES firmware

These are the MES blobs that strix (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151) ran without
problems before this image. The kernel reports them as `MES 0x80` and
`MES_KIQ 0x6f`. They come from noble
`linux-firmware 20240318.git3b128b60-0ubuntu2.21`.

The image installs them in `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/`. The kernel loads
firmware from `updates/` before `/lib/firmware/amdgpu/`, so noble firmware
updates cannot replace them.

Why they are pinned:

- The MES version is not in the file (the header field is `0`). You only see
  the version after the kernel loads the blob.
- Newer gfx1151 MES blobs have had their own bugs: 0x83 causes page faults
  (ROCm/ROCm#5724) and 0x86 causes silent hangs (ROCm/ROCm#6165).

To change a blob, boot it on strix, read the version with
`sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/*/amdgpu_firmware_info | grep MES`, run a
load test, and then update `SHA256SUMS` and the pins in `../check-image.sh`.

License: `LICENSE.amdgpu`.
```

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Build-time checks for the kairos-strix-halo-ubuntu image.
#
# Usage: check-image.sh [ROOT]   (ROOT defaults to /)
#
# The image exists for one reason: strix (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151) needs a
# kernel with the gfx1151 CWSR/VGPR fix, or the GPU hangs under ROCm load
# ("MES failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE"). This script fails the build
# if the image does not have that kernel, or if the pinned MES firmware is
# not in place. LSINITRD names the initramfs listing command (for tests).

set -eu

root=${1:-/}
root=${root%/}
lsinitrd=${LSINITRD:-lsinitrd}

fail() {
    echo "check-image: FAIL: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

for tool in zstd gzip sha256sum cmp; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "'$tool' is needed but not installed"
done

# 1. Exactly one kernel, and it is an OEM kernel.
set -- "$root"/lib/modules/*
[ "$#" -eq 1 ] && [ -d "$1" ] ||
    fail "expected exactly one kernel in /lib/modules, found: $(ls "$root/lib/modules" | tr '\n' ' ')"
kver=$(basename "$1")
case $kver in
    *-oem) ;;
    *) fail "$kver is not an -oem kernel" ;;
esac

# 2. The kernel has the gfx1151 fix. Ubuntu lists cherry-picked upstream
# commits by title in the changelog. A string search in amdgpu.ko does not
# work: unfixed kernels also contain "cwsr_size".
changelog=$root/usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver/changelog.Debian.gz
[ -f "$changelog" ] || fail "changelog not found: /usr/share/doc/linux-modules-$kver/changelog.Debian.gz"
for fix in \
    'drm/amdkfd: bump minimum vgpr size for gfx1151' \
    'drm/amdkfd: Export the cwsr_size and ctl_stack_size to userspace'; do
    gzip -dc "$changelog" | grep -Fq "$fix" ||
        fail "kernel $kver changelog does not contain '$fix'"
done

# 3. /boot/vmlinuz is the OEM kernel (Kairos boots /boot/vmlinuz).
vmlinuz=$root/boot/vmlinuz
if [ -L "$vmlinuz" ]; then
    [ "$(basename "$(readlink "$vmlinuz")")" = "vmlinuz-$kver" ] ||
        fail "/boot/vmlinuz is not vmlinuz-$kver (points to $(readlink "$vmlinuz"))"
elif [ -f "$vmlinuz" ]; then
    cmp -s "$vmlinuz" "$root/boot/vmlinuz-$kver" ||
        fail "/boot/vmlinuz is not vmlinuz-$kver"
else
    fail "/boot/vmlinuz not found"
fi

# 4. The pinned MES firmware (MES 0x80 / MES_KIQ 0x6f, see firmware/README.md).
fwdir=$root/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu
while read -r sum name; do
    [ -f "$fwdir/$name" ] || fail "pinned firmware missing: /lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/$name"
    got=$(zstd -qdc "$fwdir/$name" 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ "$got" = "$sum" ] ||
        fail "/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/$name does not match the pinned blob (got $got)"
done <<'EOF'
8e07832c18d87b7643fc221633d841a5fa3bae0e7d2aad1f2b212e190f963a0a gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst
5ad61e89d051652aada3664005df436a7694d872a5c0865eb121e03424db8588 gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst
EOF

# 5. If amdgpu loads from the initramfs, the pinned firmware must be there
# too, or early boot loads the stock blob.
```

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Kairos Ubuntu OS image for the AMD Strix Halo box (Ryzen AI Max+ 395,
# Radeon 8060S, gfx1151), with WiFi.
#
# This is kairos-wifi-ubuntu with one real change: the kernel. On the stock
# noble kernel the GPU hangs under ROCm load ("MES failed to respond to
# msg=REMOVE_QUEUE", then a GPU reset that kills every GPU process), because
# the gfx1151 compute wave save/restore (CWSR) area is sized too small. The
# fix is two amdkfd commits ("bump minimum vgpr size for gfx1151" and
# "Export the cwsr_size and ctl_stack_size to userspace"). They are in the
# Ubuntu OEM kernels, so this image installs linux-image-oem-24.04 in place of
# the kernel kairos-init picks. Without the fix, the only workaround is
# amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0.
#
# The gfx1151 MES firmware is pinned to the blobs strix ran without problems
# (MES 0x80): see firmware/README.md. check-image.sh fails the build if the
# kernel or firmware is wrong.

FROM quay.io/kairos/kairos-init:v4.3.0 AS kairos-init

FROM ubuntu:24.04 AS base-kairos
ARG VERSION=v4.3.0
ARG K8S_PROVIDER=k3s
ARG K8S_VERSION=v1.34.11+k3s1
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Pinned MES firmware. It must be in place before the init stage, because
# the init stage builds the initramfs, and amdgpu can load from it.
COPY firmware/gc_11_5_1_mes_2.bin.zst firmware/gc_11_5_1_mes1.bin.zst /lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/
COPY firmware/LICENSE.amdgpu firmware/README.md /usr/share/doc/strix-halo-mes-firmware/

# Install stage without its kernel, then the OEM kernel, then the init stage
# (which builds the initramfs for the only kernel in the image).
RUN --mount=type=bind,from=kairos-init,src=/kairos-init,dst=/kairos-init \
    /kairos-init -l debug -s install -p "${K8S_PROVIDER}" \
      --provider-k3s-version "${K8S_VERSION}" --version "${VERSION}" \
      --skip-step installKernel && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends linux-image-oem-24.04 && \
    apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    /kairos-init -l debug -s init -p "${K8S_PROVIDER}" \
      --provider-k3s-version "${K8S_VERSION}" --version "${VERSION}"

FROM base-kairos

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# WiFi userspace, the same as kairos-wifi-ubuntu: see that Dockerfile for why
# it is --no-install-recommends and why wired networking is left alone.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      network-manager wpasupplicant iw && \
    apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# One-shot NTP clock step for a WiFi-primary box (see the file).
COPY time-sync.yaml /system/oem/time-sync.yaml

# Persist saved network config across upgrades.
COPY custom_bind_mounts.yaml /system/oem/custom_bind_mounts.yaml

# Fail the build if the kernel or the MES firmware is wrong.
COPY check-image.sh /usr/local/sbin/strix-halo-check-image
RUN /usr/local/sbin/strix-halo-check-image /
```
